libraryPreparationPreflight.agent_guidance: Scope reachability metadata and the user-code filter to the io.micronaut.jdbc.* core package (not io.micronaut.configuration.jdbc.hikari, which belongs to the sibling artifact). Configure a datasource via ApplicationContext.builder().properties(...) (datasources.default.url/driver-class-name/username/password), then fetch javax.sql.DataSource and io.micronaut.jdbc.metadata.DataSourcePoolMetadataProvider/DataSourcePoolMetadata beans from the context to exercise the core abstractions directly, in addition to any standalone unit tests on classes that don't need a container.

In-memory JDBC driver needed to actually open pooled connections and exercise the core module's driver-detection and metadata code paths; same version already used by the sibling micronaut-jdbc-hikari test.

risks: Micronaut SQL submodules are normally released in lockstep from one multi-module repo, so micronaut-jdbc-hikari:7.1.0 should exist alongside micronaut-jdbc:7.1.0, but this wasn't independently verified against Maven Central in this pass — local Gradle resolution is authoritative.
If tests only call static/standalone utility classes without a live ApplicationContext, coverage of the DI-driven classes in io.micronaut.jdbc.* will be shallow even with the pool dependency present.
libraryPreparationPreflight.summary: micronaut-jdbc is the shared core/abstraction module (io.micronaut.jdbc.*: DataSourceResolver, BasicJdbcConfiguration, CalculatedSettings, pool-metadata abstractions). It registers no concrete javax.sql.DataSource bean itself — real usage always pairs it with a pool implementation (hikari/tomcat/dbcp/ucp), which are separate, non-transitive artifacts.
